lesson.subject: science
lesson.title: Plants: Roots, Flowers and Seeds
lesson.summary: What each plant part does and how flowering plants make new plants.
lesson.unit: Topic 8: Plants: roots, flowers and seeds
learning_objectives: Explain the jobs of roots, stems and leaves
Name the parts of a flower and describe pollination
Order the life cycle of a flowering plant

standards.text: Describe the functions of the parts of flowering plants; investigate how water is transported in plants; explore the role of flowers in the life cycle

success_criteria: I can say what roots, stems and leaves do
I can describe how seeds spread
lesson.real_life: Watering plants, bees in the garden and seeds that fly in the wind.

warm_up.prompt: What do plants need to make food?
warm_up.explanation: Plants use light to make food.

blocks.markdown: Today we explore how **plants** live and make seeds.
blocks.say: Welcome, young scientist! Today we find out what each plant part does and how flowering plants make new plants.

blocks.alt: A bee flying near yellow flowers on a leafy stem
blocks.caption: A flowering plant with stems, leaves and flowers.
blocks.credit: Photo by Brad Huchteman on Unsplash
blocks.say: These yellow flowers sit on a stem with leaves. Underground, the same plant has roots. Every part has a job.

blocks.markdown: **Roots** anchor the plant and **absorb** water and nutrients.
blocks.say: Roots grow in the soil. They hold the plant firmly in place, and they absorb water and nutrients.

blocks.markdown: The **stem** supports the plant and carries water upwards.
blocks.say: The stem holds the plant up. It also carries water and nutrients from the roots to the leaves and flowers.

scenes.caption: Roots absorb water.
scenes.say: Water is in the soil. The roots absorb it, and they anchor the plant too.

scenes.caption: The stem carries water up.
scenes.say: The stem carries the water up to the leaves and flowers.

question.prompt: What is the main job of the roots?
question.explanation: Roots absorb water and nutrients, and anchor the plant.

options.text: To take in water and hold the plant in the soil

blocks.markdown:
**Leaves** make food using sunlight, water and air.

Roots only take in water and nutrients.
blocks.say: Leaves make food for the plant. They use sunlight, water and air to do it. Plants do not eat the soil.

blocks.alt: Leaves use sunlight and water to make food.
blocks.caption: Leaves use sunlight and water to make food.

question.prompt: Plants make most of their food in their leaves.

blocks.title: The bee and the mustard flower
blocks.transcript: In a Punjab field, mustard flowers shine yellow in the morning sun. A bee buzzes in. She wants sweet nectar to drink. Yellow pollen sticks to her furry body as she drinks. She flies to another flower. Some pollen touches the sticky stigma. That is pollination. Now the flower can make seeds. Weeks later, the flower has made seeds in a pod. A sycamore seed spins away on its helicopter wing. It is dispersal! Far away, the seed germinates. A new plant begins!
blocks.caption: A bee carries pollen and a seed takes flight.

points: Stems carry water to the leaves
blocks.say: Remember. Roots anchor and absorb. Stems support and carry. Leaves make food.

blocks.markdown:
**Petals** attract insects.

The **stamen** makes pollen. The **carpel** makes seeds.
blocks.say: A flower has petals, which attract insects. In the middle are the stamens and the carpel.
The anther is part of the stamen. It makes pollen. The stigma is the sticky tip of the carpel. It catches pollen.

blocks.alt: A bumblebee on a yellow flower
blocks.caption: A bee carries pollen from flower to flower.
blocks.credit: Photo by Celine Lityo on Unsplash
blocks.say: This bee is visiting for nectar. Look at the pollen on its legs.

question.prompt: Which part of the flower makes pollen?
question.explanation: The anther makes and holds pollen.

blocks.markdown: **Pollination** moves pollen from an anther to a stigma.
blocks.say: Pollination is when pollen moves from an anther to a stigma. Insects and wind can carry pollen.

scenes.caption: Pollen sticks to the bee.
scenes.say: A bee lands on a flower to drink nectar. Pollen sticks to its body.

scenes.caption: Pollen reaches the stigma.
scenes.say: It flies to another flower. Some pollen touches the stigma. That is pollination.

blocks.markdown: **Seed dispersal** is how seeds spread away from the plant.
blocks.say: After pollination, the flower makes seeds. Seeds must spread away from the parent plant, so they have space to grow.

blocks.alt: Dandelion seeds with fluffy parachutes floating in the air
blocks.caption: Dandelion seeds travel on the wind.
blocks.credit: Photo by Hasan Almasi on Unsplash
blocks.say: Dandelion seeds have tiny parachutes. The wind carries them far away. Sycamore seeds spin like helicopters.

question.explanation: Dandelion seeds are carried by the wind.

blocks.markdown: The **life cycle** of a flowering plant goes round and round.
blocks.say: A seed germinates and grows into a seedling. The seedling becomes an adult plant, which flowers and makes new seeds.

scenes.caption: Seed to seedling.
scenes.say: A bean seed is planted in soil. It germinates and a root grows.

scenes.caption: Plant, flower, new seeds.
scenes.say: The seedling grows into a plant that flowers and makes new beans.

blocks.prompt: Why do seeds need to spread away from the parent plant? Have a think first.
blocks.answer_markdown: So they do not crowd each other. They need space, light and water to grow.

question.prompt: Put the plant life cycle in order.
question.explanation: A plant grows from a seed, flowers, and makes new seeds.

points: Seeds spread by wind, water and animals

blocks.say: Remember. Seeds spread by wind, water and animals. Then they germinate and the life cycle goes on.
